newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt debt may hit Y406 trln by 2005/06 -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt debt may hit Y406 trln by 2005/06 -- MOF.

text.p: Japan's outstanding government debt could increase by nearly 68 percent over the next nine years to 406 trillion yen, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
That figure could be reached if the government failed to carry out planned economic structural reforms and reduce dependency on bonds to finance the state budget, it said.
The figure, submitted to parliament's budget committee, is based on the premise that Japan's nominal economic growth will be 1.75 percent per year if reforms are not carried out.
The calculations also assume that the gap between income and revenue is funded only by public bond issues. It does not include debts of local governments.
Under this scenario, outstanding public bond issues would stand at 406 trillion yen, or 67.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), in the fiscal year beginning in April 2005.
The government expects outstanding public bond issues to amount to around 241 trillion yen at the end of March 1997.
If Japan successfully completes various reforms, nominal economic growth is expected to rise 3.5 percent per year.

Even then, outstanding government debt would still be 387 trillion yen in 2005/06. If the government managed to stop issuing deficit-financing bonds in 2005/06, the outstanding government debt would shrink to 317 trillion yen, the MOF said.
